newsitem.title: USA: Suits filed in Detroit commuter airline crash.
newsitem.headline: Suits filed in Detroit commuter airline crash.

text.p: Two suits have been filed on behalf of one of the victims of the Comair commuter plane crash near Detroit that killed 29 people, lawyers said Thursday.
The suits were filed in federal court and in state court on behalf of the family of Dexter Adams, a Procter & Gamble Co. executive from Cincinnati who died in the Jan. 9 crash.

Named as defendants in the federal suit were Comair Holdings Inc. of Erlanger, Ky., and Empresa Brasileira de Aeronautica (Embraer), the Brazilian firm that manufactured the ill-fated turbo-prop airliner.
The state suit targeted Comair Inc.,, an Ohio corporation. Comair serves as a feeder for Delta Airlines.

The suits filed earlier this week did not specify amounts for compensatory and punitive damages, attorney Stanley C. Chesley said. Chesley filed the federal suit and attorney Lawrence Hawkins Jr., a close friend of the Adams family, filed the state suit.

The crash remains under investigation by the National Transportation Safety Board and it may be several months before an official cause is determined. The lawyers said they filed the suits now in part because an Ohio law will go into effect next Monday placing limits on sums awarded in wrongful death cases.

The new law will impose caps of $35,000 in non-economic losses for each year a victim would have been expected to live under actuarial tables. At age 41, Adams was projected to live 29 more years according to the tables. He was survived by his widow and two small children.
Current Ohio law has no restrictions on such non-economic losses as sorrow and grief and loss of companionship and consortium.
Comair declined comment on the suits.
The plane crashed in a field near Detroit during a snowstorm while making an apporoach to Detroit Metropolitan Airport on a flight from Cincinnati.
